chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
"When the recipient of the gift is compensated (for it), it is not for him to return it."

key_terms.عُوِّضَ: Was compensated or given consideration in exchange

ai.seo_question: Can a recipient of a gift return it if they receive compensation for doing so?
ai.summary: In Shia jurisprudence, this hadith clarifies the distinction between a true gift (hibah) and a conditional transfer, ruling that if the recipient provides compensation to the giver to retain the gift, the transaction becomes binding and irrevocable. This principle prevents the ambiguity of 'returning' a gift when the recipient has effectively purchased their retention of it, a nuance emphasized by scholars like Al-Tusi in *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* to ensure legal certainty in family transactions.
